page: Microsoft Azure D8ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by Microsoft Hyper-V, it features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The allocation consists of 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs configured with hyperthreading (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). The processor carries a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, along with support for vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8.

The D8ns_v6 provides no bundled local ephemeral storage and does not include any hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent storage and operating system volumes rely entirely on attached network-based storage, with the instance rated as Premium Storage capable. Network optimization is integrated into the instance profile to facilitate network-bound data movement.

Benchmark outcomes show reliable mid-tier throughput across diverse workloads. The PassMark CPU score reaches 13,504.19, with multi-core stress-ng performance at 7,619.12 and single-core stress-ng at 1,900.68. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 64.69 GB/sec alongside 44.7 GB/sec write bandwidth. In data serving tests, the instance executed 10.46 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 14.07 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language tasks demonstrate varied capabilities: text generation using a small 135M parameter LLM shows strong relative output at 279.99 tokens/sec, while a 7B parameter model produces 8.08 tokens/sec, which is categorized in the bottom quartile.

The instance delivers a balanced resource profile suitable for business-critical applications requiring stable compute and memory parity without the cost overhead of dedicated local NVMe drives or GPUs. D8ns_v6 is appropriate for web serving, application backends, container hosts, relational database engines using remote storage, and moderate data processing pipelines.
